title: Isolation of Endophytic Fungi
author: Jing Xu
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jhmcj46
materials: Plant materials were thoroughly washed with running tap water, cut under sterile conditions into small pieces (2-3 cm).
Traces of sodium hypochlorite were removed by rinsing with sterile Millipore water three times (3 min each).

steps.title: Surface sterilize plant tissue
steps.instruction: Perform sequential sterilizations: dip tissue in 75 % ethanol for 1 min, then immerse in 1.3 % sodium hypochlorite solution for 3 min, and finally dip again in 75 % ethanol for 30 s.

substeps.instruction: Immerse in 1.3 % sodium hypochlorite for 3 min
Dip again in 75 % ethanol for 30 s

steps.title: Dry and remove outer tissue
steps.instruction: Dry the sterilized tissues in a sterile laminar flow hood, briefly pass them through a flame, and remove the outer tissues of the stem cuttings.

steps.title: Cut tissue into segments
steps.instruction: Using a sterile scalpel, cut the tissues into small segments of 5 mm × 5 mm.

steps.title: Confirm sterilization by imprint
steps.instruction: Make imprints of the disinfected plant fragments on PDA plates; incubate and verify that no fungal growth appears, confirming effective surface sterilization.

steps.title: Incubate segments on selective PDA
steps.instruction: Place the tissue segments on PDA plates supplemented with streptomycin, incubate at 28 °C in darkness for 2–4 weeks, and check daily for hyphal growth.

steps.title: Transfer isolates to fresh PDA
steps.instruction: Using the hyphal tip method, transfer each single fungal isolate to a fresh PDA plate.
